name: Darouiche
aliases: Chlorhexidine–alcohol versus povidone–iodine for surgical-site antisepsis
question: Does preoperative skin cleansing with chlorhexidine–alcohol prevent surgical-site infection after clean-contaminated surgery better than povidone–iodine?

design.blinding: patients and infection assessors masked; operating surgeon aware once the patient was in the operating room

arms.label: Chlorhexidine–alcohol scrub (2% chlorhexidine gluconate, 70% isopropyl alcohol)

design.population: Adults undergoing clean-contaminated colorectal, small-intestinal, gastroesophageal, biliary, thoracic, gynecologic or urologic surgery at six US university-affiliated hospitals; 849 of 897 randomized patients were in the intention-to-treat analysis.
design.description: Multicenter, patient- and assessor-blinded randomized superiority trial

verdictNote: Overall and superficial incisional infection fell; deep incisional infection P=0.05; organ-space infection did not differ.
takeaway: Skin cleansing with a 2% chlorhexidine–70% isopropyl alcohol scrub lowered 30-day surgical-site infection versus aqueous 10% povidone–iodine scrub and paint after clean-contaminated surgery in 849 adults (9.5% versus 16.1%; relative risk 0.59, 95% CI 0.41–0.85).

reports.label: Initial report
reports.citation: Darouiche RO, Wall MJ Jr, Itani KMF, et al. "Chlorhexidine–Alcohol versus Povidone–Iodine for Surgical-Site Antisepsis." *N Engl J Med.* 2010;362(1):18-26. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa0810988
reports.followUp: 30 days after surgery; weekly telephone contact after discharge

results.measure: Any surgical-site infection within 30 days (CDC criteria), intention-to-treat
results.note: Fisher's exact test, two-tailed. The per-protocol analysis (813 patients) gave similar results; Kaplan–Meier freedom from infection also favored chlorhexidine–alcohol (log-rank P = 0.004).

results.measure: Superficial incisional infection within 30 days (skin and subcutaneous tissue, excluding stitch abscesses)
results.note: P values were not adjusted for multiple testing.

results.measure: Deep incisional infection within 30 days (fascia and muscle)
Sepsis from surgical-site infection within 30 days
Any surgical-site infection after abdominal (colorectal, biliary, small-intestinal, gastroesophageal) surgery; absolute difference in percentage points (chlorhexidine–alcohol minus povidone–iodine)
results.note: Subgroup analysis; the trial was not powered for subcategories. Treatment-by-surgery-type (abdominal versus nonabdominal) interaction P = 0.41. The point difference is derived by subtraction of the two percentages.

results.measure: Any surgical-site infection after nonabdominal (thoracic, gynecologic, urologic) surgery; absolute difference in percentage points (chlorhexidine–alcohol minus povidone–iodine)
results.note: Subgroup analysis; the interval includes 0. The point difference is derived by subtraction of the two percentages.

results.measure: Any surgical-site infection after urologic surgery
results.note: Descriptive counts from Table 3; no test reported. Gynecologic surgery: 0/42 versus 1/40 (2.5%); thoracic: 2/44 (4.5%) versus 4/57 (7.0%).

harms.label: Adverse events in at least 5% of patients in either group
harms.note: Absolute difference -2.4 percentage points (95% CI -9.1 to 4.2; P = 0.49).

harms.label: Serious adverse events in more than 1% of patients in either group
harms.note: Absolute difference 1.7 percentage points (95% CI -3.3 to 6.7; P = 0.52). No serious adverse event was judged related to the study preparations.

harms.label: Preparation-related adverse events (pruritus, erythema or both around the wound)
harms.note: No serious drug-related adverse events in either group, and no fire or chemical skin burn in the operating room.

harms.label: Death within 30 days
harms.note: The four deaths with chlorhexidine–alcohol occurred in patients without surgical-site infection; the three with povidone–iodine were from sepsis due to organ-space infection. P = 0.72.

delivery.label: Skin preparation regimens
delivery.note: Chlorhexidine–alcohol: scrub with an applicator containing 2% chlorhexidine gluconate and 70% isopropyl alcohol (ChloraPrep); more than one applicator was used when the area exceeded 33 by 33 cm. Povidone–iodine: scrub followed by paint with an aqueous 10% povidone–iodine solution (Scrub Care Skin Prep Tray).

delivery.label: Randomization and analysis populations
delivery.note: Of 1003 screened, 897 were randomized; 22 and 26 did not have surgery. Per-protocol exclusions: 25 had clean rather than clean-contaminated surgery, 4 dropped out and 7 died before day 30. Randomization was 1:1, stratified by hospital, with computer-generated numbers and no blocking.

delivery.label: Systemic antibiotic prophylaxis
delivery.note: All patients received systemic prophylaxis within 1 hour before the initial incision; mean duration of preoperative administration was 1.1 days in each group.

delivery.label: Abdominal surgery
delivery.note: Colorectal 45.5% versus 43.4%, biliary 10.8% versus 12.3%, small intestinal 10.0% versus 7.7%, gastroesophageal 6.4% versus 6.6%.

delivery.label: Nonabdominal surgery
delivery.note: Thoracic 10.8% versus 13.0%, gynecologic 10.3% versus 9.1%, urologic 6.4% versus 8.0%.

delivery.label: Mean duration of surgery
delivery.note: Standard deviation 1.5 hours in each group.

delivery.label: Preoperative shower
delivery.note: Hospitals kept their existing showering practices (4% chlorhexidine gluconate, 10% povidone–iodine or triclocarban soap).
